title: Best Time to Visit Darjeeling, Month by Month
meta_description: When to visit Darjeeling: month-by-month temperatures, Kanchenjunga views, crowds and prices, plus Losar, Dashain, Tihar and what the monsoon is really like.
summary: The best time to visit Darjeeling is mid-October to early December, when skies clear after the monsoon and Kanchenjunga shows most mornings. March and April are the second window, with rhododendrons and first flush tea. June to September brings heavy rain, cloud and landslides, but also the lowest prices and the greenest gardens.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: If the mountain is the reason you are coming, come between mid-October and early December. The monsoon has washed the dust out of the air, mornings are cold and sharp, and Kanchenjunga, at 8,586 m the third highest mountain on Earth, stands clear above the town on most days. March and April are our second choice: warmer, with rhododendrons in the forests around Tiger Hill and the first flush being picked in the gardens, though haze builds as the weeks go on.

If price and quiet matter more than views, late February, early March and November are the sweet spots. July and August are the cheapest of all, and the wettest. Darjeeling receives roughly 3,000 mm of rain a year, and most of it falls between June and September.

Whatever the month, mornings are your best chance. Cloud tends to rise from the valleys by mid-morning, so the view from Tiger Hill, Observatory Hill or your hotel balcony is usually best between first light and about 9 am. Set an alarm even when you are not doing the dawn trip.

sections.heading: Month by month at a glance
paras: Temperatures are typical daily lows and highs in Darjeeling town at about 2,042 m. Tiger Hill, 500 m higher, is several degrees colder at dawn. Crowds and prices are relative to the year in Darjeeling, not to other hill towns.

sections.heading: Autumn: mid-October to early December
paras: This is the season we would choose for a first visit. After the rains end, usually by early October, the air is cleaned out and the range from Kanchenjunga to the Kabru peaks fills the northern sky. On the clearest mornings from Tiger Hill you can see Everest, Lhotse and Makalu far to the west as small pale points. Days are around 12–17 °C in October and drop below 10 °C at night by late November.

The catch is the first half of October. Durga Puja and Dashain fall then, Bengal's schools and offices close, and Darjeeling fills. Rooms double in price, the Tiger Hill road jams before dawn and shared jeeps from Siliguri sell out by mid-morning. Come in the last week of October or in November and you get the same skies with half the crowd.

sections.heading: Winter: mid-December to February
paras: Winter is cold, clear and quiet. Nights drop to 2–4 °C in town and below freezing at Tiger Hill, and few hotel rooms have central heating, so ask for a heater or extra quilts. Pack thermals, a down or thick fleece jacket, a woollen cap and gloves; the market sells cheap woollens if you forget. In exchange you get sharp mountain views most mornings, empty viewpoints and some of the year's lowest prices outside the Christmas to New Year week.

Snow in Darjeeling town is occasional, not something to plan around; some winters bring a light fall on the ridge, many bring none. Tiger Hill and the Singalila ridge above Maneybhanjan see snow more often. Losar, the Tibetan New Year, falls in February or March and brings masked dances and prayers to the monasteries at Ghoom.

January and February are also good months for birding around Lepchajagat and Senchal, when winter visitors come down from higher forests and bare branches make birds easier to spot. Shorter days mean an early dinner and early night, which suits the 4 am start for Tiger Hill.

sections.heading: Spring: March to May
paras: March and April are a fine second window. Rhododendrons flower in the forests of Senchal and on the road to Sandakphu, magnolias bloom on the lower slopes, and the gardens are picking first flush, the light, fragrant tea that sells for the highest prices. Mornings are usually clear; by noon cloud and haze rise from the plains.

May belongs to families. School holidays across India bring the year's second big rush, temperatures of 12–19 °C feel like relief after the plains, and views become a gamble as pre-monsoon cloud thickens. Book rooms and toy train joyrides early for May and June. Rabindra Jayanti, Tagore's birthday on 25 Baishakh in early May, is celebrated at his house in Mungpoo with songs and readings.

Spring is also the walkers' season. The forest trails around Senchal and Lepchajagat are dry underfoot, the Singalila ridge to Sandakphu is busy with trekkers in April and May, and village homestays at Takdah and Tinchuley are pleasant before the rains, with orchids flowering at the Takdah orchid centre from February to April.

sections.heading: Monsoon: June to September, honestly
paras: We will not pretend the monsoon is secretly the best season. From mid-June to mid-September it rains most days, sometimes for days on end, and cloud sits on the ridge so that you may not see Kanchenjunga at all in a week. Landslides cut the Hill Cart Road and the roads down to the Teesta from time to time, toy train services can be curtailed, and leeches appear on forest trails.

What you get in return is real. Hotels discount heavily, the tea gardens are at their greenest, the monsoon flush is being picked, waterfalls run full and the town belongs to the people who live in it. If you come, keep plans loose, carry a proper rain jacket rather than an umbrella, and leave a spare day before any train or flight home.
list: Keep one buffer day at the end for road closures.
Onward roads to Kalimpong and Gangtok along the Teesta have had long closures since the October 2023 Teesta flood; check current status before you travel.
Wear shoes with grip; the town's stone steps turn slick.
Expect power cuts and slow mobile data during heavy storms.

sections.heading: Festivals worth planning around
paras: Festival dates follow lunar calendars and shift each year, so check current status before you travel. These are the four we would plan a trip around.
list: Losar (February or March): the Tibetan New Year, with masked cham dances and prayers at the monasteries of Ghoom.
Dashain (September or October): the biggest Nepali festival in the hills, with family visits, red tika and swings in the villages; it overlaps Durga Puja, so book rooms early.
Tihar (October or November): the Nepali festival of lights that coincides with Diwali, with oil lamps, marigold garlands, Deusi-Bhailo songs door to door and sel roti in every kitchen.
Rabindra Jayanti at Mungpoo (early May): Tagore's birthday at the house where he stayed between 1938 and 1940.

sections.heading: Crowds, prices and booking windows
paras: Three weeks of the year account for most of the crush: Durga Puja in October, Christmas to New Year, and the middle of May to mid-June. For those weeks book rooms four to eight weeks ahead and toy train joyrides as soon as IRCTC opens them. The rest of the year you can usually find a fair room a few days out, and in July and August you can walk in and bargain.

For a budget trip with a good chance of views, our picks are the last week of October, all of November, and late February to mid-March. Room rates then sit well below the peaks, and the shared jeeps from Siliguri are easy to get.

Watch for long weekends too. Holi, Good Friday, Independence Day and the Bengali New Year in mid-April can each fill the town for three or four days, even outside the main seasons, so look at the calendar before you fix dates.

faqs.q: What is the best month to see Kanchenjunga from Darjeeling?
faqs.a: November is the most reliable month, followed by late October and early December. After the monsoon the air is clear and the mountain usually shows from dawn until mid-morning. March and early April are the second window. From June to September the mountain is often hidden for days, so do not count on views then.

faqs.q: Is December too cold for Darjeeling?
faqs.a: It is cold but manageable. Days in Darjeeling are around 8–10 °C and nights drop to 2–4 °C, colder at Tiger Hill before dawn. Pack thermals, a down or fleece jacket, a cap and gloves, and ask your hotel for a heater or extra quilts. Skies are often clear, so December rewards the cold with good views.

Only occasionally, and never on a schedule. Some winters bring a light fall on the ridge between late December and February, many bring none. Tiger Hill and higher places on the Singalila ridge, such as Sandakphu, see snow more often. If snow is the main goal, Sandakphu or North Sikkim are better bets than Darjeeling town.

faqs.q: Is it worth visiting Darjeeling in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want quiet, green tea gardens and low prices, and can live without mountain views. From June to September it rains most days, landslides sometimes close roads and toy train services can be curtailed. Keep a spare day, carry a rain jacket and check current status before you travel. Do not come for Kanchenjunga then.

faqs.q: Is Darjeeling crowded during Durga Puja?
faqs.a: Very. Durga Puja and Dashain fall in late September or October, schools and offices in Bengal close, and Darjeeling has its busiest week of the year. Rooms cost much more, shared jeeps sell out and the Tiger Hill road jams before dawn. Book four to eight weeks ahead, or come in the last week of October instead.

faqs.q: When is the cheapest time to visit Darjeeling?
faqs.a: July and August are the cheapest, with heavy monsoon discounts on rooms. For low prices with a decent chance of views, choose late February to mid-March or November outside any long weekend. The most expensive weeks are Durga Puja, Christmas to New Year and mid-May to mid-June, when room rates rise by a third or more.

faqs.q: When is first flush tea season in Darjeeling?
faqs.a: First flush is usually picked from March into April, after the bushes wake from winter. Second flush, with the fuller muscatel taste, follows in May and June. Garden visits are most interesting in these months because you can see plucking and processing. The exact dates depend on the weather and vary by garden each year.

faqs.q: When is Losar celebrated at Ghoom?
faqs.a: Losar, the Tibetan New Year, falls in February or early March, following the Tibetan lunar calendar, so the date changes every year. The monasteries around Ghoom hold prayers and, in some years, masked cham dances in the days around it. Check current status before you travel and ask the monastery about visitor timings.

faqs.q: Is April a good time to visit Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Yes. April brings mild days of about 10–17 °C, rhododendrons in the Senchal forests, first flush tea and clear early mornings, although haze and cloud usually build by late morning. Crowds are moderate until the school holidays begin in May, and room prices are fair. It is a good month for families and walkers.
